meta.title: Report a suspect: Cybercrime Report & Tracking
meta.description: This category is not built in this prototype. Here's what it is, why it isn't built, and what to actually do right now.

report-suspect.title: Report a suspect to I4C, or report abuse to a social platform
report-suspect.subtitle: You want to flag a suspicious number, account, or website to the authorities, or report abusive content to the platform hosting it.
report-suspect.whatThisIsBody: This covers two related but different actions: reporting a suspect (a number, account, website, or app used in cybercrime) to I4C so it can be added to the Suspect Repository, and reporting abusive content directly to the social media platform that hosts it, using that platform's own reporting tools.
report-suspect.notBuiltBody: Neither of these is built on this prototype. Reporting a suspect to I4C needs access to the real repository we don't have; reporting abuse to a platform depends on that platform's own systems, not ours.
report-suspect.whyBody: The idea is simple: you should be able to check a thing before you trust it, and report a thing after you don't. What is missing here is the data behind it, the real repository is built from complaints across the whole country, and we have no access to it. Rather than invent entries, we built the parts we could stand behind and named the rest. See <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Report abusive content on the platform itself
steps.body: WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, X, and YouTube each have their own in-app report button. That report goes straight to the platform and works today, right now.

steps.title: Report the suspect on the real portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a dedicated flow for reporting a suspect number, account, or website to I4C.

steps.title: File your own complaint if you're a victim
steps.body: If this suspect took money from you, our one finished journey covers writing it up and getting a Complaint ID.

report-suspect.moneyNote: If the suspect you're reporting also took money from you, our one finished journey covers that part.

volunteer-account.title: Cyber volunteer registration, login, and terms
volunteer-account.subtitle: You want to create a Cyber Volunteer account, sign in to one, or read the volunteer terms and conditions.
volunteer-account.whatThisIsBody: The real Cyber Volunteer Programme is a genuine account system: citizens register, get verified, and are approved before they can take part. It has its own login, its own terms and conditions, and its own vetting process.
volunteer-account.notBuiltBody: Registration, login, and a real terms-of-service document all need an account and verification system this prototype doesn't build. Inventing a fake login here would be exactly the fake interactivity this project refuses to ship.
volunteer-account.whyBody: The idea is simple: you should be able to check a thing before you trust it, and report a thing after you don't. What is missing here is the data behind it, the real repository is built from complaints across the whole country, and we have no access to it. Rather than invent entries, we built the parts we could stand behind and named the rest. See <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Read what the real programme actually is
steps.body: Our Cyber Volunteer Concept page explains the real programme honestly, without pretending this prototype runs it.

steps.title: Register on the real portal
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in has the real volunteer registration, login, and terms and conditions.

steps.title: Call 1930 if something feels off
steps.body: If a message or call claiming to be about volunteer registration asks for money or your Aadhaar/PAN, treat it as a scam and report it.

volunteer-account.moneyNote: If someone impersonating the volunteer programme took money from you, our one finished journey covers that part.

daily-digest.title: Daily digest
daily-digest.subtitle: You want a daily summary of newly published cyber-security advisories and trends.
daily-digest.whatThisIsBody: The real portal publishes a daily digest of newly reported advisories and trends, refreshed every day.
daily-digest.notBuiltBody: Building this honestly would mean either connecting to a real, live incident feed we don't have, or inventing today's numbers ourselves. We refuse to do the second one, so there is no digest here, not a fake one with made-up figures.
daily-digest.whyBody: The idea is simple: you should be able to check a thing before you trust it, and report a thing after you don't. What is missing here is the data behind it, the real repository is built from complaints across the whole country, and we have no access to it. Rather than invent entries, we built the parts we could stand behind and named the rest. See <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Read our general advisories instead
steps.body: Our Advisories page covers common, ongoing scam patterns that don't depend on today's date, so it can't go stale or be faked.

steps.title: See the real daily digest
steps.body: cybercrime.gov.in publishes the actual day-by-day advisory digest.

daily-digest.moneyNote: If a scam mentioned in an advisory already cost you money, our one finished journey covers filing a report.

screen-reader.title: Dedicated screen reader tool
screen-reader.subtitle: You're looking for a built-in screen-reader tool like the one on the real portal.
screen-reader.whatThisIsBody: The real portal offers a dedicated screen-reader tool bundled into the page that reads content aloud on request.
screen-reader.notBuiltBody: We didn't build a separate screen-reader tool. Instead, every page here is built with semantic HTML, labelled controls, and visible focus states, so your own screen reader, NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, or TalkBack, already works properly, without us needing to bundle one.
screen-reader.whyBody: The idea is simple: you should be able to check a thing before you trust it, and report a thing after you don't. What is missing here is the data behind it, the real repository is built from complaints across the whole country, and we have no access to it. Rather than invent entries, we built the parts we could stand behind and named the rest. See <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Use your device's own screen reader
steps.body: NVDA or JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on Mac and iOS, TalkBack on Android, all work correctly on this prototype.

steps.title: Read our accessibility statement
steps.body: It lists exactly what's implemented and what hasn't been independently verified yet, honestly.

screen-reader.moneyNote: If you're here to report money that was taken from you, our one finished journey is built to work with a screen reader end to end.

public-notices.title: RTI and CPGRAMS public notices
public-notices.subtitle: You're looking for Right to Information disclosures or CPGRAMS grievance-redress notices published by the department.
public-notices.whatThisIsBody: RTI (Right to Information) public notices and CPGRAMS (Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System) notices are official disclosures a government department is legally required to publish.
public-notices.notBuiltBody: We're an independent hackathon prototype, not a government department. We have no real notices to publish, so we won't invent any to fill this space.
public-notices.whyBody: The idea is simple: you should be able to check a thing before you trust it, and report a thing after you don't. What is missing here is the data behind it, the real repository is built from complaints across the whole country, and we have no access to it. Rather than invent entries, we built the parts we could stand behind and named the rest. See <link>what's real and what's mocked</link>.

steps.title: Use the official RTI and CPGRAMS channels
steps.body: These disclosures are handled by the real government department, not by this prototype, which has no legal standing to publish them.

steps.title: See what this prototype actually is
steps.body: Our what's real vs mocked page states plainly that we are an independent, unaffiliated hackathon build.
